THIS ONE IS NOT A BACKLOG AND THE ORIGINAL CEILING WAS MIS-SPECIFIED, not merely too low. `unlinked_events` is `count(*) from events where duplicate_of_id is null and city_id is null` (99991790194100:524) -- an INFLOW counter that rises with every ingested event whose city does not resolve and falls when run_event_city_link (cron `5 3 * * *`) drains it overnight. Measured across three consecutive daily snapshots it read 743 / 742 / 744, and the activation ceiling was pinned at the exact snapshot value with ZERO headroom, which makes it a coin flip that reds every open PR in the repo at random -- it did exactly that on 2026-09-26 when two events arrived with no resolvable city. The new ceiling is derived, not chosen: 744 currently unlinked + 90 days of the measured residue rate. Residue rate measured 2026-09-26 -- of the 744, only 12 were created in the trailing 30 days (0.4/day) while 727 came from a burst 30-90 days ago, so 0.4/day is normal accrual and 90 days of it is 36. A genuine producer regression is a step change of hundreds (that 727-event burst is the shape), so 36 of headroom still catches one while absorbing daily noise. `operations.unlinked_venues` carries the IDENTICAL defect and is green only by luck, because it happens to be falling (3584 -> 3534 -> 3518 over the same three snapshots); it is left alone here rather than pre-emptively loosened, but it is the same coin flip the day that trend reverses.
